subject.title: fix(feishu): pace outbound sends per target

question: Should OpenClaw accept a Feishu-owned, default-off `sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs` config contract for proactive per-account/per-target outbound pacing once real proof or an explicit proof override is available?
rationale: Source inspection supports the Feishu-plugin-local design, but adding a new user-facing config key and deciding whether mock seam proof is enough requires maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Feishu Pacing
options.body: Review this PR or a replacement toward default-off per-account/per-target Feishu send pacing after real proof or an explicit proof override is available.

options.title: Keep Reactive Retry Only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and document that Feishu delivery relies on existing retry/backoff after rate-limit responses.

options.title: Defer To Broad Rate Limiting
options.body: Leave the Feishu-specific request open or close it into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13615 if maintainers want only a cross-provider limiter.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Feishu Pacing
recommendation.body: Review this PR or a replacement toward default-off per-account/per-target Feishu send pacing after real proof or an explicit proof override is available.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the community-maintained Feishu/Lark plugin owner candidate for Feishu-specific outbound behavior.
